A5 cells as a ggplot2 layer

geom_a5.Rd

Draws A5 cells from a cell column, with any ggplot2 fill scale. Works with coord_cartesian(), coord_quickmap() and coord_sf(), and combines with geom_sf() layers in the same plot.

Usage

geom_a5(
  mapping = NULL,
  data = NULL,
  ...,
  render = c("auto", "vector", "raster"),
  raster_dpi = 300,
  na.rm = FALSE,
  show.legend = NA,
  inherit.aes = TRUE
)

Arguments

mapping

Aesthetic mappings. cell is required: an a5_cell vector, hex strings, or an a5R::a5_covering vector, drawn as the cells each covering stores (uncompact it first to draw its cells at one resolution). fill, alpha, colour, linewidth and linetype are understood.

data, show.legend, inherit.aes, na.rm, ...

As for other ggplot2 layers.

render

"auto" (default) draws polygons, switching to a raster when cells are smaller than a few device pixels. "vector" and "raster" force one mode. Cell borders (colour) need vector mode, so "auto" stays vector when they are set.

raster_dpi

Pixel density for raster mode on vector devices (PDF, SVG), which have no pixels of their own. Bitmap devices use their own resolution.

Value

A list of a ggplot2 layer and a default coord_sf(), as geom_sf() returns.

Details

Like geom_sf(), the layer comes with a default coord_sf(): its crs is taken from the plot's sf layers, or is EPSG:4326 when there are none, so the map keeps a fixed geographic aspect ratio. Adding any coord replaces it.

Large cell sets are drawn as a raster: each device pixel takes the colour of the cell containing its centre. This is exact at the output resolution and its cost depends on the number of pixels, not cells.
